title: DirtyFileGuard singleton is shared across forked agents
evidence: fork() calls get_guard().recapture() which mutates the module-level singleton. Forked child agents and the parent share the same guard reference, so recapture in a fork affects the parent's guard.
why_it_matters: Child/fleet sessions need independent guard baselines to track per-session dirty file snapshots. Without this, a fork child recapturing its dirty state corrupts the parent's protected file list.
best_practice_anchor: Session-scoped mutable state should not be shared across forked runtimes. Each session should own its DirtyFileGuard instance.
recommended_action: Introduce per-session DirtyFileGuard instances or a GuardRegistry keyed by session_id. Replace the module-level singleton with session-scoped guard lifecycle.

title: clear_history() recaptures guard state instead of preserving conversation-only snapshot
evidence: clear_history() calls _reset_session() which calls get_guard().recapture(). A conversation-only reset should not invalidate the dirty file snapshot because no filesystem mutations occurred.
why_it_matters: clear_history is a conversation-level operation (trim old messages). Recapturing the guard on conversation reset loses the original dirty file baseline and may allow overwriting protected files that were dirty at mission start.
best_practice_anchor: Conversation lifecycle and runtime lifecycle are separate concerns. Resetting chat history should not reset filesystem guards.
recommended_action: Split clear_history into conversation-only reset (preserves guard snapshot) and full session reset (recaptures guard). Or add a preserve_guard parameter.
unblocks: safe clear_history during long-running sessions with dirty files

title: checkpoint and coordination tools have UNKNOWN determinism and mutation metadata
evidence: test_builtin_tools_have_explicit_metadata fails: checkpoint has ToolDeterminismClass.UNKNOWN and ToolMutationClass.UNKNOWN; coordination has ToolDeterminismClass.UNKNOWN and ToolMutationClass.UNKNOWN. Both tools were added by a parallel agent without completing determinism/mutation classification.
why_it_matters: UNKNOWN metadata breaks the contract that all built-in tools have explicit determinism and mutation classification. This blocks tool-level evidence instrumentation and makes dogfood session analysis unreliable for these tools.
best_practice_anchor: Every built-in tool must have explicit ToolDeterminismClass and ToolMutationClass values per the tool contract coverage test.
recommended_action: Classify checkpoint as deterministic_repo_state + writes_workspace (creates commits). Classify coordination as deterministic_repo_state + writes_workspace (writes coordination store). Update both tool classes with explicit metadata.
suggested_slice: Complete checkpoint and coordination tool metadata

title: search_replace.py has recurring PLR0914 (too many locals) and PLR0915 (too many statements) pressure
evidence: Ruff PLR0914 fires on search_replace.py run() method with >15 local variables. The method handles SEARCH/REPLACE parsing, file I/O, fuzzy matching, block application, and evidence emission in one function. Multiple missions have hit this lint pressure without fixing it.
why_it_matters: PLR0914/PLR0915 indicate functions doing too much in one scope. This makes the tool harder to reason about, test, and safely modify. It also creates merge pressure when multiple agents touch the same large function.
best_practice_anchor: PEP 8 and Ruff PLR0914: extract helper methods for distinct phases. Group related locals into typed dataclasses or small value objects.
recommended_action: Decompose run() into phase helpers: _parse_blocks(), _apply_blocks(), _emit_evidence(). Consider a small SearchReplaceResult value object to group block counts and per-file hashes.
unblocks: reduced merge conflicts on multi-agent work
